extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for non-statistical peer reviewers on how to identify statistical problems in research manuscripts and when to request specialist statistical review. Covers common problem categories and a brief reviewer checklist of actions to take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request specialist statistical review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should request specialist statistical review when they encounter: insufficient detail in methods or results; common statistical issues; interpretation not based on the presented evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers lack the expertise to assess statistical components, they are encouraged to recommend specialist statistical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power issues
rubrics_metrics.description: No sample size calculation; underpowered analyses; post-hoc power calculations (often misleading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for pre-specified sample size calculations tied to primary outcomes; be cautious of post-hoc power statements which are often uninformative. Underpowered analyses can give false negative results or unstable estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Using parametric tests on non-normal data without checking assumptions; applying t-tests when ANOVA needed; multiple comparisons without correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether assumptions (e.g., normality, homoscedasticity) have been assessed and whether the chosen test matches the data structure and study design. Look for appropriate correction or control when multiple tests/comparisons are performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome reporting bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective reporting of significant outcomes; switching primary outcome between protocol and paper; composite outcomes hiding negative individual results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare reported outcomes to protocols/registrations when available; be alert to emphasis on statistically significant secondary outcomes while downplaying prespecified primary outcomes; examine composite outcomes for masking of unfavorable component results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confounding and adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to adjust for known confounders; over-adjustment (controlling for mediators); 'garden of forking paths' — too many analytic decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the set of covariates is appropriate (not omitting known confounders and not adjusting for mediators). Watch for excessive, ad hoc analytic choices that increase risk of spurious findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-value abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Overemphasis on p < 0.05; confusing statistical and clinical significance; 'trending toward significance' language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage interpretation that considers effect sizes and confidence intervals, not p-values alone; flag language that implies importance based solely on arbitrary thresholds or 'trends'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cherry-picking subgroups; multiple comparisons not corrected; drawing causal inferences from observational subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether subgroup analyses were pre-specified and whether corrections for multiple testing are applied; be cautious about causal claims from subgroup findings, especially in observational data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignoring missingness; inappropriate imputation; no sensitivity analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for description of the extent and patterns of missing data, justification for chosen handling methods (e.g., complete-case vs imputation), and sensitivity analyses exploring robustness to missing-data assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-event analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to account for censoring; incorrect proportional hazards assumptions; no competing risks analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure survival analyses appropriately handle censoring, verify whether proportional hazards assumptions were tested and reported, and consider whether competing risks methods are needed when events preclude each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: No appropriate gold standard; spectrum bias; no confidence intervals on sensitivity/specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an appropriate reference standard was used, whether the sample represents the full clinical spectrum (avoid spectrum bias), and whether uncertainty (e.g., CIs) is reported for performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods described in sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether statistical methods are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that models, variable definitions, handling of missing data, clustering, adjustments, software/packages, and any decisions affecting analyses are described so a knowledgeable reader could reproduce or assess the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis matches the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the analysis matches the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the chosen estimands, outcomes, populations, and statistical methods align with the stated objectives or hypotheses (e.g., per-protocol vs intention-to-treat, population-level vs individual-level inference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions are checked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit tests, diagnostics, or justification that key statistical assumptions (normality, linearity, proportional hazards, independence, etc.) hold or that alternative methods were used when they do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty is quantified
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that uncertainty is quantified (CI or SE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect effect estimates accompanied by confidence intervals or standard errors to convey precision; be wary of reliance on point estimates or p-values without interval estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for selective reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for signs that only significant analyses or outcomes are presented; compare methods/results sections for evidence of unreported analyses and check consistency with protocols or trial registries when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag for specialist statistical review when uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag for specialist statistical review when uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the above checks raise concerns or if the reviewer lacks confidence in assessing the statistical methods or their appropriateness, explicitly recommend formal statistical review by a specialist.
